start.content:
The Master sees things we often miss. We saw a tree; He saw a tragedy of missed purpose.
+ [You mean the lack of fruit?]
    Exactly. In our scriptures, the fig tree is often a symbol for our nation. To have the appearance of vitality—the green leaves—but to be barren when the Lord is hungry... it's a sobering thought.
    -> symbolism
+ [Peter seems shaken.]
    Peter focuses on the power. I am trying to understand the sign. Why now? Why this road?
    -> temple

symbolism.content: A tree that produces leaves but no fruit is deceptive. It's a performance. The Master has no patience for religious performance that doesn't feed the soul.

temple.content:
We just left the Temple where He drove out the merchants. Now He withers a barren tree. The two acts are linked, friend. He is declaring that the season of empty ritual is coming to an end.
+ [And what comes next?]
    A house of prayer for all nations. A kingdom built on fruit, not just leaves.
    -> DONE
